frames.narration: Alice sends 30 to Bob. Her app made the transfer id t-5521 once and will reuse it on every retry. The wallet API hashes the sender's wallet id to find shard 2.
The request goes to the one writer that owns Alice's wallet. It handles requests one at a time, so no lock is needed.

The writer has not seen t-5521 and Alice has 120, which is at least 30. It appends one event, 'debited 30 for t-5521', together with an outbox entry for Bob, in a single atomic write. Her balance is now 90 and she gets her confirmation after about 5 ms.
The outbox entry is published on the stream, keyed by Bob's wallet. The 30 is now in flight: gone from Alice, not yet in Bob. It is recorded durably, so it cannot vanish.
Bob's writer, on shard 7, reads the entry. It has not applied t-5521, so it appends 'credited 30 for t-5521' and records the id. Bob's balance goes from 200 to 230.

Suppose Bob's writer crashed before it acknowledged the entry. The stream delivers it again. The writer recognises the id, changes nothing, and acknowledges, so Bob is credited exactly once and nothing is in flight any more.
Bob's phone is told about the 30 within a fraction of a second of the credit.

At night the reconciler replays each partition's events and checks that they match the stored balances, that every debit has a credit or a refund, and that the total equals deposits minus withdrawals. Alice lost 30 and Bob gained 30, so nothing was created or lost.
